title: Rose water and pistachio cake
subtitle: a fragrant, moist sponge with ground pistachios and a rose water drizzle
excerpt: Rose water and pistachio cake is a light sponge scented with rose water and made with a mix of plain flour and ground pistachios. The rose water is delicate rather than floral; the pistachios give the crumb a soft nutty note and a faint green tint. A thin rose water icing drizzled over the cooled cake sets to a crisp, fragrant glaze.
sourceNotes: Rose water as a cake flavouring documented in British and Middle Eastern baking from at least the eighteenth century. The pistachio and rose water combination is particularly associated with Persian and Turkish pastry traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the uniced sponge, well wrapped, for up to 2 months. Defrost and add the icing on the day of serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 days.

content.text: Rose water and pistachio cake is a light, moist sponge scented with rose water and made with pistachios blitzed to a fine crumb. The rose water flavour is gentle; use a good-quality culinary rose water rather than one marketed for cosmetics. The pistachio crumb gives the cake a slightly green-tinted crumb and a soft, nutty flavour.

items.prepNote: shelled, blitzed to a fine crumb

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease a 20 cm round cake tin and line the base with baking paper.
Blitz the pistachios in a food processor until they form a fine crumb. Mix with the flour and baking powder.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes with a stand mixer or electric hand whisk. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Stir in the rose water.
Fold in the flour and pistachio mixture in two additions, alternating with the milk, until just combined. Do not over-mix.
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 32 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Leave to cool in the tin for 10 minutes before turning out onto a rack.

Once completely cool, mix the icing sugar with the rose water and 1 to 2 teaspoons of cold water until you have a thick, pourable icing. Drizzle over the cake and scatter with chopped pistachios if using. Leave to set for 20 minutes before serving.

attrs.problem: Rose water flavour undetectable after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid the cheapest rose water; diluted products lose most of their flavour in the oven.
attrs.fix: Use good-quality culinary rose water and add the full amount in both the batter and the icing. The icing is where the rose flavour comes through most clearly.

attrs.problem: Cake dense and heavy rather than light
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-mixing once the flour goes in; too much stirring develops the gluten and makes the sponge tough.
attrs.fix: Fold the flour in with a spatula using as few strokes as possible, stopping as soon as the last streak of flour disappears.
